pass_a_gloss: [...] creation [are] the things in Christ, because also a new root has been laid down; and he has become also a second Adam; and not, just as that one, joint cause of wrath and of the turning away from above for those having come from him, but rather procurer and giver of the closeness toward God, through sanctification and incorruption and the righteousness in faith. These things the wise Paul explains to us through the passage set before [us]: therefore as through one man, he says, the sin entered into the world, and through the sin the death, and so the death went through into all men, on which all sinned; for the death slipped in, as I said, through the sin in the first-formed and in the beginning of the race; then the whole race in order was grazed over. But also the dragon, the finder of the sin, having been strong in Adam by the ways of the badness, has made the mind of man walkable: For all bent away, together they became useless. Having come, then, away from the face of the all-holy God, because the mind of man lies set carefully upon the evil things from youth, we lived through a more irrational life; and the death, having been strong, swallowed, as the prophet says, and also Hades widened its soul and opened its mouth so as not to leave off; for since we have become imitators of the transgression in Adam, in which all sinned, we have been swept under the equal penalties with him; but the [world] under heaven has not remained without help, for the sin has been pulled down, the Satan has fallen, and the death too has been made idle. For until law sin was in world. The law through Moses was, as I said, a proof of the weakness of those stumbling, not able to loose sin; but rather it was working out wrath; for there was necessity that those transgressing be borne under the penalties marked out in law; and where at all [there is] a manner of transgression, there somewhere wholly is also sin. And if indeed sin is procurer of death, it is in some way all necessity to say that the death which sprang up from it is strengthened together with it, and that, when it has been pulled down, it is wholly shaken down together, and perishes along with it as with its own mother. So sin was until law, he says, in world: for while the law still lay [in force], the charges of the transgression also were being made strong against those stumbling; but now that it is idle, the indictment for transgressing has ceased with it; and when the sin has ceased, as I said, the death too will cease with it. But the death reigned from Adam until Moses, and the rest. But if this, in what manner, someone might say, did death overpower those on the earth even before law? For even if some did not become liable to the transgressions of the law, because the law had not yet been laid down, yet they too went under the corruption upon the likeness of the transgression of Adam; it is like as if he were perhaps saying: the death running over, according to the likeness of Adam, all the race from him, just as when a plant has suffered harm at the root, it is in some way all necessity that the branches having come from it wither. pass_b_english: …creation is what is in Christ (2 Corinthians 5:17), because a new root has been set in place; and he has become the second Adam (1 Corinthians 15:45–47). He is not, like the first, the cause of wrath and of heaven's turning away for those born of him; rather, he procures and gives closeness to God, through sanctification, incorruption, and the righteousness that is by faith. The wise Paul explains this to us in the passage before us. So he says: “As through one man sin entered the world, and death through sin, and so death spread to all men, because all sinned” (Romans 5:12). For, as I said, death slipped in through sin in the first-formed man, at the beginning of the race; then it overran the whole race in turn. Moreover the dragon, the inventor of sin, having prevailed in Adam by the ways of wickedness, made the human mind a road he could tread: “For all have turned aside, together they have become worthless” (Psalm 14:3; Romans 3:12). So, having gone out from the presence of the all-holy God, because the human mind is intently set “on evil from youth” (Genesis 8:21), we lived a life more like that of brute beasts. And “death, having grown strong, swallowed up,” as the prophet says (Isaiah 25:8), and “Hades enlarged its appetite and opened its mouth without ceasing” (Isaiah 5:14). For since we became imitators of the transgression in Adam, in that all sinned, we came under the same penalties as he did. But the world under heaven has not been left without help: sin has been pulled down, Satan has fallen, and death too has been abolished.

“For until the law sin was in the world” (Romans 5:13). The law given through Moses was, as I said, an exposure of the weakness of those who stumble, not a release from sin; rather, it brought about wrath (Romans 4:15). For those who transgressed had to come under the penalties set down in the law; and wherever there is any form of transgression at all, there sin surely is too. And if sin brings about death, we must surely say that the death which sprang from it shares its strength, and that when sin is pulled down death is shaken down with it and perishes together with it, as with its own mother. So, he says, sin was in the world until the law: for while the law still stood, the charges of transgression held firm against those who stumbled; but now that it has become inactive, the indictment for transgressing has ceased along with it. And once sin has ceased, as I said, death too will cease with it.

“Yet death reigned from Adam to Moses,” and so on (Romans 5:14). But if so, someone might ask, how did death gain the mastery over those on earth even before the law? For even if some were not liable for transgressions of the law, since the law had not yet been given, they too still came under corruption after the likeness of Adam's transgression. It is as if he were saying: death overran the whole race that came from Adam, in the likeness of Adam; just as, when a plant has been harmed at its root, the shoots that grew from it must all wither. κτίσις τὰ ἐν Χριστῷ, ὅτι καὶ ῥίζα τέθειται καινή· γέγονε δὲ καὶ δεύτερος Ἀδάμ· καὶ οὐχ
ὥσπερ ἐκεῖνος ὀργῆς παραίτιος καὶ ἀποστροφῆς τῆς ἄνωθεν τοῖς ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεγονόσι,
πρόξενος δὲ μᾶλλον καὶ δοτὴρ τῆς πρὸς Θεὸν οἰκειότητος, δι' ἁγιασμοῦ τε καὶ
ἀφθαρσίας καὶ τῆς ἐν πίστει δικαιοσύνης. ταῦτα ἡμῖν ὁ σοφὸς ἐξηγεῖται Παῦλος διὰ τῆς
προκειμένης ῥήσεως· οὐκοῦν ὡς δι' ἑνὸς ἀνθρώπου φησὶν ἡ ἁμαρτία εἰς τὸν κόσμον
εἰσῆλθε, καὶ διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος, καὶ οὕτως εἰς πάντας ἀνθρώπους ὁ θάνατος
διῆλθεν ἐφ' ᾧ πάντες ἥμαρτον· εἰσέδυ μὲν γὰρ, ὡς ἔφην, διὰ τῆς ἁμαρτίας ὁ θάνατος ἐν
τῷ πρωτοπλάστῳ καὶ ἐν τῇ τοῦ γένους ἀρχῇ· εἶτα ὅλον ἐφεξῆς κατενεμήθη τὸ γένος.
ἀλλὰ καὶ ὁ τῆς ἁμαρτίας εὑρετὴς δράκων ἰσχύσας ἐν Ἀδὰμ τοῖς τῆς φαυλότητος τρόποις,
βατὴν εἴργασται τὴν ἀνθρώπου διάνοιαν· "Πάντες γὰρ ἐξέκλιναν, ἅμα ἠχρειώθησαν."
ἐκ προσώπου δὴ οὖν γεγονότες τοῦ παναγίου Θεοῦ διά τοι τὸ ἐπιμελῶς ἐγκεῖσθαι τὴν
ἀνθρώπου διάνοιαν "ἐπὶ τὰ πονηρὰ "ἐκ νεότητος," ἀλογώτερον διέζωμεν βίον· καὶ
"κατέπιεν "μὲν ὁ θάνατος ἰσχύσας," ὡς ὁ προφήτης φησὶν, ἐπλάτυνε δὲ καὶ "ὁ ᾅδης τὴν
ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ διήνοιξε τὸ στόμα "αὐτοῦ τοῦ μὴ διαλιπεῖν·" ἐπειδὴ γὰρ τῆς ἐν Ἀδὰμ
παρα 183 βάσεως γεγόναμεν μιμηταὶ καθ' ὃ πάντες ἥμαρτον, ταῖς ἴσαις ἐκείνῳ δίκαις
ὑπενενήγμεθα· ἀλλ' οὐ μεμένηκεν ἀνεπικούρητος ἡ ὑπ' οὐρανὸν, καθῄρηται γὰρ ἡ
ἁμαρτία, πέπτωκεν ὁ σατανᾶς, κατήργηται δὲ καὶ ὁ θάνατος. Ἄχρι γὰρ νόμου ἁμαρτία
ἦν ἐν κόσμῳ. Ὁ νόμος ὁ διὰ Μωυσέως, ἔλεγχος ἦν, ὡς ἔφην, τῆς τῶν πταιόντων
ἀσθενείας, οὐ λυτικὸς ἁμαρτίας· κατειργάζετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὀργήν· ἦν γὰρ ἀνάγκη τοὺς
παραβαίνοντας ταῖς ἐν νόμῳ διωρισμέναις ὑποφέρεσθαι δίκαις· οὗ δὲ δὴ ὅλως
παραβάσεως τρόπος, ἐκεῖ που πάντως καὶ ἁμαρτία. καὶ εἴπερ ἐστὶν ἁμαρτία θανάτου
πρόξενος, πᾶσά πως ἀνάγκη συνεῤῥῶσθαι λέγειν αὐτῇ καὶ τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς ἀναφύντα
θάνατον· καθῃρημένῃ τε πάντως συγκατασείεσθαι, καὶ οἷά περ ἰδίᾳ συνδιολλύσθαι
μητρί· ἦν οὖν ἄχρι νόμου ἁμαρτία φησὶν ἐν κόσμῳ· κειμένου γὰρ ἔτι τοῦ νόμου, καὶ τὰ
τῆς παραβάσεως ἐγκλήματα κατὰ τῶν πταιόντων ἐκρατύνετο· ἀργοῦντος δὲ ἤδη,
πέπαυται σὺν αὐτῷ τοῦ παραβαίνειν ἡ γραφή· πεπαυμένης δὲ τῆς ἁμαρτίας, ὡς ἔφην,
συμπεπαύσεται καὶ ὁ θάνατος. Ἀλλ' ἐβασίλευσεν ὁ θάνατος ἀπὸ Ἀδὰμ μέχρι Μωσέως
κ.τ.λ. Ἀλλ' εἰ τοῦτο, τίνα τρόπον φαίη τις ἂν κατεκράτησε τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς καὶ πρὸ
νόμου θάνατος; εἰ γὰρ καί τινες οὐ γεγόνασι ταῖς τοῦ νόμου παραβάσεσιν ἔνοχοι, διά τοι
τὸ μήπω τεθεῖσθαι τὸν νόμον, ἀλλ' ὑπέδυσαν καὶ αὐτοὶ τὴν φθορὰν ἐπὶ τῷ ὁμοιώματι
τῆς παραβάσεως Ἀδάμ· ὅμοιον ὡσεὶ λέγοι τυχόν Ἐπιτρέχοντος τοῦ θανάτου καθ'
ὁμοιότητα τὴν Ἀδὰμ τὸ ἐξ αὐτοῦ πᾶν γένος, ὥσπερ φυτοῦ παθόντος βλάβος εἰς ῥίζαν,
πᾶσά πως ἀνάγκη τοὺς ἐξ αὐτοῦ γεγονότας μαραίνεσθαι κλῶνας. τύπον γεμὴν αὐτὸν
τοῦ μέλλοντος εἶναί 184 φησι, τουτέστι Χριστοῦ, καίτοι παραγεγονότος ἤδη, καὶ τῆς

revisions.summary: Pass A, lemmas, choices and bible_refs rebuilt from the Greek to match the reviewed English; pass_b_english is the current English.

review_notes: Old draft rewrote rather than translated: 'The creation is rooted in Christ' for 'what is in Christ is a new creation'; it dropped the contrast with the first Adam as cause of wrath; repeated Psalm 14:3 three times and placed it before its context; mistranslated Genesis 8:21 ('carefully placed on evil things') and ἀλογώτερον διέζωμεν βίον ('contrary to God's will'); left out Isaiah 25:8 and 5:14; invented 'until sin was spoken of' and 'the writing of transgressions' for Cyril's reading of ἄχρι νόμου and ἡ γραφή (the indictment); dropped the strength-and-mother image and the closing type-of-Christ clause (Romans 5:14). Retranslated with inline citations; both edges marked with ellipses. Closing edge: 'καὶ τῆς | μετὰ σαρκὸς οἰκονομίας διαπεράναντος τὸ μυστήριον' is one participial clause ('and had brought to completion the mystery of the economy in the flesh'), so u02-open now ends '…had brought to completion the…'; the rv1 reviewer of u02-rem-early should open with '…mystery of his saving work in the flesh' (its current first sentence 'After the mystery had been fully passed through…' misparses this seam). Old translator_notes ('aims to provide a coherent reading') are worksheet debris and should be dropped.
Opens mid-sentence, continuing the end of u01-rem-close.
